- When sentiment is high (≥0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >+5% from prior day), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +3% above prior peak.
- If sentiment is low (≤0.25) and price is falling, model underestimates; add 0.5–1% to forecast to avoid premature bottoming.
- Model consistently underestimates in early 30-day horizon (first 5–7 days); apply +0.5–1.5% bias to first 5 days if sentiment is neutral or negative.
- If sentiment history shows repeated “0.00” or “0.20” values, model exhibits mean reversion bias; adjust forecast to align with recent 5-day average if no strong sentiment signal.
- When sentiment is high but price is falling, model often fails to recognize reversal; reduce forecast slope by 20–30% for next 3–5 days.
